parity_risks.note: A macro is a workflow, not a tool: there is no cookbook pattern for `macro`, only for the tools inside clean_codes.yxmc. Its sub-DAG is inlined one CTE per inner tool, and a change to the .yxmc file changes this segment even though inventory.yxmd did not change.
The question MinQty is 1 in the parent's <Value name="MinQty">, overriding the macro's own NumericUpDown default of 0. Translating the default instead would keep every zero-quantity row.

The macro's RegEx is Replace with CopyUnmatched, so a SKU that does not match is kept as it was rather than becoming NULL. REGEXP_REPLACE already returns the subject unchanged on no match, so the two agree -- but a translator who reached for a CASE with an ELSE NULL would not.

The macro's RegEx is case-INSENSITIVE (Alteryx spells the attribute CaseInsensitve), so `ab 12` and `zz9` normalise; the parent's RegEx at tool 3 is case-sensitive. The two flags are opposite and easy to swap.

The macro's Filter is [QTY] >= 1 and a NULL QTY makes that NULL, which is not true, so those rows leave on the unwired False anchor. That is what keeps a NULL WAREHOUSE (and a NULL SKU) out of the Cross Tab downstream, which is why SKU, WAREHOUSE and QTY are declared NOT NULL on this stream.

Snowflake's regex dialect is not Python's, which is what the simulator uses: \d and \s are ASCII-only in the local engine and Unicode-aware in the oracle, and case-insensitive [A-Za-z] folds differently at the edges of Unicode. No golden set contains a non-ASCII digit or a non-breaking space, so the divergence is recorded rather than guarded against.
